sections.h2: Selling in Maplewood: the order of steps
sections.html:
Maplewood adds a local step before anything else: a Truth-in-Sale of Housing evaluation has to be done before the house is shown. After that you choose an agent, a sale on your own or a cash buyer. The evaluation sits on top of Minnesota's disclosure rules, and it sets how fast you can go to market.

The city is in Ramsey County, on the northern and eastern edge of Saint Paul, about ten minutes' drive from downtown. The latest estimate of 40,717 residents is 3.2 percent below the 2020 count. Owners hold 71.8 percent of homes. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $323,200, rent is $1,406 and household income is $91,394, across 15,210 households.

  • Agent listing: evaluation first, then showings with the report on display.
  • Owner sale: same city report, plus your own disclosures and contract.
  • Cash sale: the buyer purchases in present condition, and the report is still part of the file.

Single-family houses, duplexes, townhouses, condominiums and other attached one-family units need a full report before they can be shown. A duplex needs a report for each unit. Manufactured homes are not covered. The city's Truth-in-Sale page has the program details.

You call a city-licensed evaluator yourself, since each evaluator sets fees and availability. The evaluator files a copy with the city and gives you one, which you keep on display for buyers. A copy must go to the buyer before a contract is signed, and the report is valid for one owner or one year.

The owner also signs a statement covering:

  • Flooding, sewer backup or chronic water seepage the owner knows about, and its cause and extent.
  • Pending housing orders from the city, and whether the home has a homestead classification.
  • Known wells, with a map, and whether each is in use or sealed.
  • Deed restrictions, shoreland, pipeline or floodplain rules, and an adjacent high-voltage transmission line.

The report is for disclosure, and the sale does not depend on the deficiencies it lists. City inspectors may still use it to require correction of code violations.

Before you sign an agreement to sell, Minnesota Statutes 103I.235 requires a written statement that you know of no wells, or a statement and map showing each well and whether it is in use, not in use or sealed. At closing, a well disclosure certificate goes to the recorder unless the deed carries the standard no-wells statement.

The county recorder collects $54 for a completed certificate. A seller who knew of an undisclosed well can owe the sealing costs and attorney fees if the buyer sues within six years of closing. Individual condominium units are exempt. If you are unsure whether an old well exists on your lot, check your survey and deed records before you sign.

Ramsey County splits the bill into a May 15 payment and an October 15 payment, and a weekend due date rolls forward to the next business day. Real property tax of $100 or less must be paid in full by May 15. A homestead penalty starts at 2 percent on the day after the first half is due and climbs to 4 percent on June 1.

The county allows a one-time penalty waiver once every ten years for each parcel, applying to either the first or the second half. Hardship abatement requests go to the Auditor/Treasurer's office at 651-266-2222. Valuation questions go to the county assessor at 651-266-2131.

The assessor's estimated market value is set as of January 2 for taxes payable the following year. If you sell in the second half of the year, ask the closing agent how the October installment will be divided, since the purchase agreement controls it.

Since 2019 Maplewood has required a rental license before tenants move in, with a background check on each owner and an on-site inspection. Properties are placed on a one-, two- or three-year inspection cycle.

If you are selling a rental that holds a license, bring your inspection history to the table, because a buyer who plans to keep renting will want it. Call the city at 651-249-2300 to confirm what a new owner must file.

sections.h2: How to line up the evaluation
sections.html:
Book the evaluator early. Compare quotes and ask how soon a report can be filed, since showings cannot begin until it exists. Walk the house first and fix the cheap items, so the report is shorter. If the report lists problems, you can repair them, leave them for the buyer to handle or price them into an as-is sale. A cash buyer will read the same report and adjust the offer.

Keep the filed copy where visitors can see it, and give the buyer their copy before any contract is signed. Missing that step can delay the whole sale.

sections.h2: What a cash sale means in Maplewood
sections.html: A cash buyer purchases the house in its present condition, but the city report still has to exist, so book the evaluator first. The advantage is speed and certainty: you skip the lender's appraisal, repair negotiations and most showings. Ask for the offer in writing with a firm closing date, then compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and carrying costs. On closing day the title company records the deed and pays any mortgage and taxes owed from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Does Maplewood require an inspection before I can list my house?
faqs.a: Yes. A city-licensed evaluator must complete a Truth-in-Sale of Housing report before the property is shown. It covers houses, duplexes, townhouses and condominiums, and you call the evaluator directly to book it.

faqs.q: How long does a Maplewood TISH report last?
faqs.a: One owner or one year. The city's director can also require a new inspection if there is substandard maintenance or later damage to the building.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair everything on the Maplewood report before selling?
faqs.a: No. The sale does not depend on the deficiencies listed, though inspectors may use the report to require correction of code violations later.

faqs.q: What are the Ramsey County payment dates for a Maplewood home?
faqs.a: May 15 and October 15. A homestead pays a 2 percent penalty if the first half arrives after May 15, and Ramsey offers a one-time waiver per parcel every ten years.

faqs.q: What does a Maplewood rental license cost?
faqs.a: The annual fee is $150 plus $50 per unit, and each owner passes a background check and an inspection before the license is issued.
